EU AI Act transparency practice

One Article 50 practice. Four ways to act.

Use the technical layer you need or move through the full engagement: diagnose the touchpoint, apply the duty, implement the disclosure and document the company position.

01

Scope the Article 50 touchpoint

Scan the public page, identify the AI interaction and establish which system and role need analysis.

02

Apply the transparency duty

Translate the relevant Article 50 duty into clear wording, timing and placement for the real interaction.

03

Deploy the notice layer

Use the badge, WordPress, Shopify or Wix implementation path and verify the rendered disclosure.

04

Document the company position

Map systems, classifications, duties, evidence gaps and next actions in one specialist-reviewed assessment.

The scanner, notice, plugins, badge and implementation guidance are the technical methods. The €99 assessment adds the specialist company-wide analysis and written evidence plan.

Book a call

Contents of the assessment

Six sections. One clear action plan.

A consistent, reviewable structure tailored to the systems your company operates.

01

Your AI inventory

A single inventory of the AI systems your company operates, including customer-facing tools, internal systems and third-party services.

02

Risk classification per system

Each system mapped to its relevant category: prohibited, high-risk under Annex III, transparency-only under Article 50, or out of scope.

03

What you must disclose, exactly

For each relevant touchpoint: what to disclose, where to place the notice, when people must see it and which languages to use.

04

Your evidence position

The records a regulator, enterprise client or insurer may request, the evidence available today and the gaps to close.

05

Prioritised action plan

Required actions ordered by urgency and impact, with clear owners, dependencies and target dates.

06

Specialist review

A named specialist's conclusion on your current position, the first action to take and any point that should be referred to legal counsel.

Charged once, per company. Not a subscription.

Procedure

From intake to action plan

Step 1

You describe your company

Add your business, sector, operating countries and known AI systems. Uncertain or missing systems are part of the review.

Step 2

We assess your case

Your systems, website and sector are reviewed against the regulation and current guidance. Each system is classified and its obligations are stated individually.

Step 3

You receive the written assessment within 24–48h

Receive the inventory, classifications and prioritised action plan. If delivery misses the window, the fee is refunded in full.

On the reports that the AI Act was delayed

The postponement covered the high-risk rulebook: Annex III obligations moved to December 2027 and Annex I to August 2028. Article 50 transparency obligations remain on schedule from 2 August 2026. The assessment establishes which timetable and duty applies to each system.
